query: What kinds of hardware issues appear in these incidents?

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: The manner in which the hardware fails (connectivity, malfunction, power issue, display issue, physical damage) is a genuine aspect OF a hardware hiccup -- it decomposes WHAT the issue is, a constitutive part-of relationship.

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: The scope/locus of what is affected (individual workstation, department server, network service, infrastructure) is a constitutive aspect of the incident -- it characterizes the WHERE/WHAT-is-impacted dimension of the hardware issue rather than externally predicting it.

per_column.name: severity_indicator
per_column.rationale: Despite the name suggesting severity, its values (configuration_request, connectivity_issue, intermittent_failure, degraded_performance, critical_outage) mix issue-type restatements that heavily overlap failure_mode (connectivity_issue vs connectivity, degraded_performance vs performance_degradation). It largely restates the failure-mode facet rather than isolating a clean severity aspect, so it is not a distinct constitutive facet.

judge.rationale: failure_mode and affected_scope are legitimate, non-overlapping facets of a hardware hiccup (the type of fault and the scope of impact). However, severity_indicator's value space collapses into failure_mode categories (connectivity, degraded performance) rather than representing a clean orthogonal severity axis, creating substantial overlap and lowering mutual exclusivity. A true severity facet (a real intensity/urgency dimension) would have improved exhaustiveness; as implemented it is a restatement. The set covers 'what fails' and 'what is affected' but leaves an intended severity/impact-intensity aspect only muddily captured, so coverage is moderate.
